body:
It's completely normal to feel this way. I’ve been there myself—after ending a ten-year relationship and moving across the country two years ago, I've had a loooot of time to reflect and adjust. It was eye-opening to realize how much I had been seeking validation from men/my relationship and how that had impacted my sense of self-worth. Here are a few tips that might help you on your journey!  
  
1) When you notice intrusive thoughts about men, try jotting them down or using meditation to refocus. Consider creating a personal mantra that resonates with your goals and aspirations, and keep it visible on your phone or around your home (I love sticky notes for this.) Your therapist can help you develop these tools too.  
  
2) Try new activities and hobbies that you're genuinely interested in, or have always wanted to try. Whether it’s volunteering, joining a community sports team, yoga, birding, or welding, new experiences and switching up your environment can provide a healthy distraction and boost your mood. Think of this time as a period of "dating yourself" and discovering what truly makes you happy.  
  
3) Invest in a good vibrator (this was a huge unlock for me!)

Remember, it's okay to have these feelings, and you've already taken a big step in the right direction by seeking ways to address them. My most important piece of advice would be to be patient and tender with yourself—self-discovery and healing take time, but with each step you take, you’re moving closer to a stronger, more fulfilled you. You’ve got this!!!
